introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Economics 3 (0725), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Duration: 1 hour 45 minutes.**

INSTRUCTIONS TO CANDIDATES: Answer ANY THREE questions. All questions carry equal marks. You are advised to spend the first fifteen minutes reading the paper. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: The following is an individual's demand function for apples in a certain daily market: $Q_d = 1200 - P$, where $Q_d$ is quantity demanded in units and $P$ is price in FCFA.

Question 2(b)(ii) : le sujet ne dit pas que les 10 acheteurs sont identiques ; c'est l'hypothèse nécessaire à la dérivation et le corrigé l'énonce.

Aucun total n'est imprimé par question (« All questions carry equal marks ») : `points` de l'exercice est laissé vide ; les points de chaque sous-question (a), (b)... sont la somme des points imprimés de ses parties ; la somme des points imprimés de la question vaut 20.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Briefly define an individual's demand function. (2 marks)

(ii) Establish the individual's demand schedule for a price range of 1000 FCFA to 500 FCFA, given that price of apples is changing by 100 FCFA. (5 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Individual demand function.** It is an **equation that expresses the quantity of a good that one consumer is willing and able to buy as a function of its price** (other determinants such as income and tastes being held constant). Here $Q_d = 1200 - P$ shows that quantity demanded falls by one unit whenever the price rises by 1 FCFA.

**(ii) Demand schedule.** Start at $P = 1000$ and reduce the price by 100 FCFA at each step down to 500 FCFA. Substitute each price into $Q_d = 1200 - P$:

| Price per apple $P$ (FCFA) | Working | Quantity demanded $Q_d$ (units) |
|---|---|---|
| 1000 | $1200 - 1000$ | 200 |
| 900 | $1200 - 900$ | 300 |
| 800 | $1200 - 800$ | 400 |
| 700 | $1200 - 700$ | 500 |
| 600 | $1200 - 600$ | 600 |
| 500 | $1200 - 500$ | 700 |

Each 100 FCFA fall in price raises the quantity demanded by 100 units, so the schedule shows the inverse relationship between price and quantity demanded (the law of demand); plotted, it gives a downward-sloping straight-line demand curve.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Now assume that there are 10 buyers of apples in the market referred to in (a) above,

(i) Define a market demand function. (2 marks)

(ii) Derive a market demand function for apples in this market. (3 marks)

(iii) Determine the price per apple that will enable producers to sell 5,000 apples. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i) Market demand function.** It is an **equation showing the total quantity of a good demanded by all the consumers in the market at each price**; it is obtained by adding the individual demand functions horizontally (summing the quantities demanded by all buyers at each price).

**(ii) Derivation.** The 10 buyers are assumed to be identical, each with $Q_d = 1200 - P$. Market demand is the sum of the ten individual quantities:

$$Q_D = 10 \times Q_d = 10\,(1200 - P)$$

$$Q_D = 12\,000 - 10P$$

**(iii) Price for 5,000 apples.** Put $Q_D = 5000$:

$$5000 = 12\,000 - 10P \quad\Rightarrow\quad 10P = 12\,000 - 5000 = 7000 \quad\Rightarrow\quad P = 700$$

Producers can sell 5,000 apples at a price of **700 FCFA per apple**. Check: at 700 FCFA each buyer demands $1200 - 700 = 500$ apples, and $10 \times 500 = 5000$.

questions.enonce_markdown: State two concepts which can be used to explain why more apples will be demanded at a lower price than at a higher price. (4 marks)
questions.corrige_markdown:
Two concepts (2 marks each, with explanation):

1. **The law of diminishing marginal utility** - as a consumer eats more apples, the extra satisfaction (marginal utility) from each additional apple falls. A consumer will only buy additional apples if the price is lower, because the price he or she is willing to pay is equal to the (falling) marginal utility.
2. **The income and substitution effects of a price change** - when the price of apples falls, apples become cheaper relative to other fruits (substitution effect: consumers switch towards apples) and consumers' real purchasing power rises (income effect: they can afford more apples). Both effects increase the quantity demanded.

Another acceptable concept: new buyers enter the market at the lower price (the market-size effect).
